From Wiktionary, the free dictionary
See also: planché

English

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Borrowed from French planche (“board”). Doublet of phalange, phalanx, planch, plancha, and plank.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /plɑːnt͡ʃ/
  • (General American) IPA(key): /plænt͡ʃ/
  • Rhymes: -ɑːnʃ, -ɑːntʃ

Noun

[edit]

planche (plural planches)

  2. (gymnastics) A position where the gymnast is horizontal and face-down, using only the hands as support.
    Hyponym: Maltese cross

Related terms

[edit]
  • planchet
  • planchette
  • plank

Translations

[edit]
position where the gymnast is horizontal and face-down
  • Chinese:
    Mandarin: 水平支撐 / 水平支撑 (shuǐpíng zhīchēng)
  • Finnish: nojavaaka
  • French: planche (fr) f
  • Polish: deska (pl) f
  • Portuguese: please add this translation if you can
  • Spanish: plancha (es) f
  • Turkish: planche

planche

Danish

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Borrowed from French planche, from Latin phalanga.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /planɡsjɘ/, [ˈpʰlɑŋɕɘ]

Noun

[edit]

planche c (singular definite planchen, plural indefinite plancher)

  1. plate (illustration)
  2. poster

Inflection

[edit]

nominative planche planchen plancher plancherne

French

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Inherited from Old French planche, from Vulgar Latin planca, contracted from palanca, from Latin phalanga, from Ancient Greek φάλαγξ (phálanx).

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /plɑ̃ʃ/
  • Audio:(file)
  • Audio (Paris):(file)
  • Audio (Switzerland (Valais)):(file)
  • Audio (France (Vosges)):(file)
  • Audio (France (Vosges)):(file)
  • Audio (France (Lyon)):(file)
  • Audio (France (Somain)):(file)

Noun

[edit]

planche f (plural planches)

  1. board
  2. spread (picture covering a whole page)
  3. plank
  4. woodcut
  5. board (used for sport, e.g. skateboard or surfboard)
  6. (figuratively) plank, beanpole (very thin person)

Derived terms

[edit]
  • avoir du pain sur la planche
  • monter sur les planches
  • planche à beurre
  • planche à découper
  • planche à laver
  • planche à pain
  • planche à repasser
  • planche à roulettes
  • planche à voile
  • planche apéro
  • planche de salut
  • planche pourrie

Descendants

[edit]
  • → Catalan: planxa
  • → Czech: planš (“piste”)
  • → Danish: planche (“poster”)
  • → English: planche
  • → Italian: plancia
  • → Portuguese: prancha
  • → Sicilian: plancia
  • → Spanish: plancha (“iron, plank”)
    • → Central Bikol: plantsa
    • → Cebuano: plantsa
    • → English: plancha
    • → Maguindanao: pilinsa
    • → Tagalog: plantsa

Verb

[edit]

planche

  1. inflection of plancher:
    1. first/third-person singular present indicative/subjunctive
    2. second-person singular imperative

See also

[edit]
  • planchiste
  • planche à voile

Further reading

[edit]
  • “planche”, in Trésor de la langue française informatisé [Digitized Treasury of the French Language], 2012

Old French

[edit]

Alternative forms

[edit]
  • planke, planque

Etymology

[edit]

From Vulgar Latin planca, contracted from palanca, from Latin phalanga, possibly through the influence of planus. The Latin term derives from Ancient Greek φάλαγξ (phálanx).

Noun

[edit]

planche oblique singular, f (oblique plural planches, nominative singular planche, nominative plural planches)

  1. plank; board (piece of wood)

Descendants

[edit]
  • Anglo-Norman: planke (see there for further descendants)
  • Bourguignon: plainche
  • Champenois: piainche
  • French: planche (see there for further descendants)
  • Norman: plianche, plaunque
  • Picard: planque

References

[edit]
  • Frédéric Godefroy (1880–1902), “planche”, in Dictionnaire de l’ancienne langue française et de tous ses dialectes du IXe au XVe siècle […], Paris: F[riedrich] Vieweg; Émile Bouillon, →OCLC.

planche

    1. first/third-person singular present subjunctive
    2. third-person singular imperative
